verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Figures are 100 minus the 2023 resistance percentages given in the paper's narrative (pages 3 and 8), not read from the mislabelled table columns. The aminoglycoside class result (30.12% susceptible, 69.88% resistant) is not shown because no single agent is named. Per-year figures exist for 2014 to 2023 (for example 2014, n=27: carbapenem resistance 3.70%, ceftriaxone 7.41%). Other uropathogens (E. coli 9,211, P. aeruginosa 1,108, A. baumannii 192, S. aureus 161, enterococci, Proteus) are counted in the paper without susceptibility data.

notes: Neelambike Sumana et al. (Front Microbiol 2025) report a retrospective study of Klebsiella pneumoniae from urine at JSS Medical College and Hospital, Mysuru, a 1,800-bed hospital, tested by VITEK 2 with CLSI breakpoints. Of 920 isolates from 2014 to 2023, only the 83 from 2023 are shown. The paper's Tables 3 and 4 have the S and R headers swapped (the column labelled S holds % resistant), as its own text and carbapenem-resistant counts confirm, so figures are 100 minus the resistance figures in the text and intermediate counts as susceptible. Carbapenems are one class figure (61.5%; 38.55% resistant, 32 of 83) shown for ertapenem, imipenem and meropenem alike; the ciprofloxacin figure is the paper's fluoroquinolone row, and the cefuroxime figure is oral cefuroxime axetil. Carbapenem resistance peaked at 66.13% in 2021 and was 41.84% (385 of 920) over the decade.

notes.imipenem: Pooled carbapenem-class figure (per table footnote). Derived: 100 - 38.55% resistance. Table S/R columns mislabeled/swapped; resistance value confirmed by paper narrative and CRKP counts (32/83).
notes.meropenem: Pooled carbapenem-class figure; not species-specific. Derived from 38.55% resistance.
notes.ertapenem: Pooled carbapenem-class figure; not species-specific. Derived from 38.55% resistance.
notes.ciprofloxacin: Footnote defines fluoroquinolones = ciprofloxacin. Derived: 100 - 40.96% resistance.
notes.cefuroxime: Parenteral cefuroxime: 100 minus 85.54% resistant in 2023 (paper narrative).

excluded.why: oral cefuroxime axetil (100 minus 91.57% resistant) printed beside parenteral cefuroxime; both map to one drug key, so the parenteral figure is kept

focus: Klebsiella pneumoniae from urine in 2023 (83 of 920 isolates from 2014 to 2023)
